title.en: Show a sample as one draw, not as the distribution

summary: Make randomness reproducible and repeatable so a point cloud reads as one realisation among many.
objective: Prevent a single random sample from being presented as the underlying distribution.
applies_when: Random points, trials or paths are generated and displayed.
A statistic such as a mean or a proportion is computed from generated data.
The scene animates repeated sampling or a convergence story.
example_prompts: Draw a sample and let me redraw it to see how much it varies.
Show many samples and the distribution of their means.
negative_signals: Fixed measured data sets, which are one sample but not regenerable.
not_for: Fixed measured data sets, which are one sample but not regenerable.

principles: A cloud of points is one realisation. Presented once, it invites the viewer to read its accidental features, such as a gap or a cluster, as properties of the distribution.
Reproducibility and variability are both needed: a fixed seed lets a result be discussed, and redrawing shows how much of the picture was noise.
Animating a smooth approach to a limit misrepresents randomness. Real repeated sampling wanders, and that wandering is the phenomenon.
Sample size must be visible, because almost every judgement a viewer makes about a cloud depends on it.
implementation: Use an explicit seeded generator, display the seed, and provide a redraw control that changes only the seed.
Display the sample size prominently and make it adjustable, so the effect of size is discoverable rather than asserted.
Where a limiting distribution is shown, draw it as a separate reference object rather than as something the sample turns into.
For repeated sampling, accumulate the statistic across draws and show its distribution, which is the honest form of the convergence story.
Keep the reference distribution and the sample visually distinct so a viewer never has to guess which is which.
observable_checks: Redraw with the same seed and confirm an identical sample, then redraw with a new seed and confirm the draw is independent. Do not require the picture to look different every time: a small discrete or nearly degenerate population can legitimately repeat, and the check is that the seed changes and the draw is redrawn, not that the image changes.
Increase the sample size and confirm the reported statistic stabilises while individual draws still vary.
Confirm the reference distribution does not change when the sample is redrawn.
Check that any claimed convergence is shown as a distribution of statistics rather than as a smooth animation.

creative_affordances: Presentation of samples as points, particles, physical objects or accumulating stacks is a free choice.
A deliberately dramatic single draw is fine when the viewer can immediately draw another.
known_limits: Authored guidance about presenting randomness; it asserts no distributional result.
It does not evaluate the quality of any particular pseudo-random generator.
